anomalies.description: Thruster-2 chamber pressure dropped 18% below nominal during the last burn sequence and has not recovered. Valve position sensor shows erratic readings. Fuel line temperature is elevated. Possible partial blockage or valve actuator failure. Situation is active and unresolved.

Avionics bay temperature has been rising steadily for the past 25 minutes, now 6.8 degrees above the upper nominal operating limit. Primary cooling loop flow rate nominal. Secondary loop appears to have reduced throughput. No automatic fault has triggered yet but trend is continuing upward.

Battery cell group C shows a voltage imbalance of 0.31 V between the highest and lowest cells. Charge controller has applied a balancing current but imbalance persists. State of charge is nominal. Pattern consistent with early cell degradation; not yet safety-critical but warrants ground review.

data_products.description: Thruster-2 fault log captured 8 seconds ago at the moment chamber pressure first fell below the safety threshold. Contains valve command history, pressure sensor timestamps, and actuator response latencies. Direct evidence for the active ANOM-017 propulsion anomaly.

Thruster-2 valve actuator fault record, collected 22 seconds ago. Documents three consecutive failed valve position commands during the anomaly window. Includes actuator drive current waveform and motor temperature readings. Critical for root-cause determination of ANOM-017.

Thruster-2 chamber pressure telemetry snapshot captured during the active ANOM-017 anomaly window, 45 seconds ago. Pressure trace shows a step-down event followed by oscillation. Essential for understanding whether the fault is a sensor failure or a real fluid system event.

Thruster-2 fuel line pressure and temperature diagnostic collected 70 seconds ago. Covers the fuel inlet, combustion chamber, and nozzle throat sensor array. Allows ground team to distinguish a blockage scenario from a valve actuator fault in ANOM-017.

Propulsion system vibration envelope diagnostic from the inertial sensor suite, sampled during the ANOM-017 event window. Vibration amplitude at thruster-2 is 3.4x nominal. Data required to assess structural stress accumulation. Collected 90 seconds ago.

Complete thruster controller diagnostic log for the 10-minute window spanning the ANOM-017 detection event. Includes command sequences, telemetry polling intervals, watchdog resets, and internal state machine transitions. Collected 110 seconds ago.

Thruster-2 chamber pressure telemetry stream for the 5-minute period immediately before and during the ANOM-017 onset. Sampled at 10 Hz. Provides the ground team with full pressure history needed to assess anomaly progression. Collected 55 seconds ago.

Thruster-2 valve position telemetry during the ANOM-017 anomaly window. Position readings oscillate between 14% and 67% commanded open instead of holding at 40%. Shows the valve is responding but with severe hysteresis. Collected 80 seconds ago.

Thruster power draw telemetry during and after the ANOM-017 event. Power draw is 22% higher than predicted for the observed thrust output, consistent with actuator working against a mechanical obstruction. Collected 105 seconds ago.

Thruster-2 fuel line temperature telemetry collected during ANOM-017. Inlet temperature 11 degrees above nominal, consistent with a partial blockage causing localized heating. This is a key diagnostic discriminator between a blockage and a valve fault. Collected 60 seconds ago.

Thruster-2 nozzle and combustion chamber thermal profile snapshot taken 30 seconds ago during the active anomaly. Chamber wall temperature nominal. Nozzle throat temperature 4% elevated. Indicates the pressure drop is upstream of the nozzle.

Command acknowledgment record for the last 15 thruster-2 control commands sent during the ANOM-017 window. Three commands show timeout, six show unexpected partial execution. Confirms ground command uplink was received but spacecraft execution was anomalous. Collected 50 seconds ago.

Avionics bay temperature telemetry for the past 30 minutes, sampled at 1 Hz. Shows the steady upward trend associated with ANOM-021. Current reading is 6.8 degrees above nominal upper limit. Trend analysis needed to predict when automatic safe-mode threshold will be reached. Collected 18 seconds ago.

Secondary cooling loop flow rate and inlet/outlet temperature differential for the avionics bay, collected 35 seconds ago. Flow rate is 28% below nominal, explaining the reduced heat removal capacity driving ANOM-021. Key diagnostic for assessing whether the fault is a pump degradation or a flow restriction.

Flight computer processor die temperature telemetry during the ANOM-021 avionics heating event. Processor temperature 4.1 degrees above baseline. If the trend continues, automatic thermal throttling will reduce computing capacity within approximately 12 minutes. Collected 42 seconds ago.

Thermal control system diagnostic report for the secondary cooling loop, generated 120 seconds ago in response to ANOM-021. Includes pump speed logs, valve states, and bypass configuration. Needed to determine whether ground intervention can restore normal loop throughput before safe-mode threshold is reached.

Avionics bay thermal model residuals diagnostic: comparison of measured temperatures against the predicted values from the spacecraft thermal model. Residuals indicate an unexpected 31 W heat source in the avionics bay that is not accounted for. Collected 95 seconds ago during ANOM-021 investigation.

Avionics bay housekeeping snapshot: processor load (74%), memory usage (61%), storage I/O, watchdog timer state, and internal bus health. Collected 28 seconds ago during the ANOM-021 elevated-temperature condition. Provides system context for ground assessment of current operational margins.

Battery cell group C voltage telemetry for the past 2 hours, sampled every 30 seconds. Shows the progressive imbalance growth associated with ANOM-034. The 0.31 V differential is visible as a slow divergence over time. Useful for characterizing degradation rate. Collected 40 seconds ago.

Battery cell group C temperature and internal resistance measurements collected 55 seconds ago. Cell resistance elevated by 8% relative to initial calibration, consistent with the cell degradation hypothesis for ANOM-034. Resistance increase correlates with temperature cycling history.

Battery charge controller output telemetry during the ANOM-034 balancing operation. Shows the applied balancing current and its effect on cell voltages over the last 25 minutes. Balancing is active but voltages have not converged. Collected 70 seconds ago.

Power subsystem diagnostic report triggered by ANOM-034: full battery pack health assessment including capacity fade estimate, cycle count, and projected remaining lifetime. Collected 140 seconds ago. Large dataset but contains trending information needed for mission planning.

Solar array power generation telemetry cross-referenced with battery state-of-charge during the ANOM-034 window. Solar harvest nominal. The imbalance is therefore isolated to the cell group itself and is not a charging input issue. Collected 180 seconds ago.

Power subsystem housekeeping snapshot: total bus voltage, load currents by subsystem, battery state-of-charge (87%), solar array output, and regulator health. Collected 15 seconds ago. Routine context for ground power management; ANOM-034 cell imbalance is flagged in this record.

Solar array panel-level current and voltage telemetry collected 600 seconds ago during nominal operations. All 12 panels performing within 2% of predicted output. Routine power health data; not related to any active anomaly.

Power distribution unit load telemetry, collected 1200 seconds ago. Documents current draw per subsystem during the previous science observation sequence. Useful for long-term power budget calibration. Low urgency.

Battery group A and B cell voltage telemetry over the past 4 hours. Both groups nominal, no imbalance detected. Provides the baseline for comparison with the anomalous group C behavior in ANOM-034. Collected 2400 seconds ago.

Fuel cell supplementary power unit telemetry collected 3600 seconds ago. Unit in standby mode. Output voltage and temperature nominal. Routine engineering verification that backup power is available. Low urgency.

Full spacecraft thermal survey collected 480 seconds ago: 48 temperature sensors across all subsystems. Most readings nominal except the avionics bay anomaly already flagged as ANOM-021. Useful as baseline context for understanding the scope of the heating event.

Propulsion module thermal history for the past 3 hours, sampled every 2 minutes. Shows the thermal buildup in the thruster-2 area that preceded ANOM-017. Provides long-term context beyond the immediate fault window. Collected 1800 seconds ago.

Science payload thermal telemetry collected 900 seconds ago. Detector focal plane assembly temperature stable at 185 K. Cryocooler operating within specification. No thermal issues in science payload. Routine downlink confirmation.

Reaction wheel assembly thermal telemetry for the past 2 hours. Wheel bearing temperatures nominal. No thermal trending concerns. Collected 2400 seconds ago. Routine maintenance data for ground archive.

Communications subsystem thermal telemetry covering transponder, high-gain antenna feed, and RF amplifier temperatures. All readings nominal. Collected 1500 seconds ago during routine downlink pass preparation.

High-gain antenna pointing error telemetry for the current contact pass: measured boresight deviation is 0.12 degrees from predicted. SNR degraded by approximately 1.8 dB from budget. Affects current downlink rate. Collected 25 seconds ago. Needed for ground pointing correction.

Transponder RF telemetry: transmit power, received signal level, carrier lock status, and modem frame error rate for the current contact window. Frame error rate is 0.7%, slightly above nominal 0.3%. Collected 18 seconds ago. Useful for link quality assessment.

High-gain antenna subsystem diagnostic collected 90 seconds ago: includes pointing mechanism encoder data, drive motor telemetry, and control loop error signals. Pointing deviation likely caused by attitude control coupling during the last maneuver. Needed for antenna controller reconfiguration assessment.

Previous contact window link statistics: total data transmitted, retransmission count, forward error correction throughput, and contact duration. Collected 2700 seconds ago. Useful for contact planning but not urgent.

Command uplink statistics for the past 24 hours: total commands received, checksum errors (0), rejected commands (0), and last valid command timestamp. All nominal. Routine ground operations data. Collected 3600 seconds ago.

Communications subsystem housekeeping packet: transceiver power state, antenna deployment status, command decoder health, and telemetry formatter status. All nominal. Collected 12 seconds ago. Essential baseline for understanding the current link health.

Thrusters 1, 3, 4 operational telemetry during and after the ANOM-017 event. All three secondary thrusters nominal. Provides the baseline against which thruster-2 degradation can be measured. Collected 130 seconds ago.

Propellant tank pressure and temperature telemetry for the main oxidizer and fuel tanks. Both tanks nominal pressure. Fuel tank temperature elevated by 3 degrees compared to pre-anomaly baseline, consistent with the ANOM-017 heat signature. Collected 160 seconds ago.

Propulsion subsystem housekeeping: valve configuration states, latch states, pressure regulator settings, and fill-drain valve status for all four thrusters. Collected 20 seconds ago. Configuration context required for interpreting ANOM-017 fault data.

Current spacecraft state vector from onboard orbit determination: position, velocity, and covariance matrix for the navigation epoch 45 seconds ago. Required for planning the next maneuver sequence. Accuracy is within 120 m radial, which is within mission requirements but at the upper tolerance boundary.

Delta-V budget and trajectory correction maneuver planning data from the onboard navigation filter, 60 seconds ago. The ANOM-017 propulsion event has introduced a small trajectory perturbation. Ground verification is needed before the next scheduled burn window in 8 hours.

Star tracker catalog match telemetry: 142 matched stars against the onboard catalog during the current pointing sequence. Attitude accuracy estimated at 0.008 degrees, within specification. Collected 70 seconds ago. Used for navigation filter input.

Ground station range and range-rate tracking residuals from the previous contact arc. Residuals well within noise floor, consistent with the onboard state vector. Provides independent verification of navigation accuracy. Collected 2400 seconds ago.

Attitude determination solution at epoch 50 seconds ago: quaternion, angular rates, and pointing error relative to the science target. Current pointing error is 0.015 degrees, within the 0.02 degree science requirement. Navigation state is healthy.

Inertial measurement unit gyroscope telemetry for the past 20 minutes. Angular rate noise and bias drift within calibration limits. No gyroscope anomalies detected. Collected 80 seconds ago. Routine attitude determination support data.

Reaction wheel assembly speed and torque telemetry for the current observation sequence. Wheels 1–3 nominal. Wheel 4 approaching momentum saturation at 82% of maximum. Desaturation maneuver may be required within 4 hours. Collected 65 seconds ago.

Reaction wheel 4 momentum accumulation diagnostic: documents the torque disturbance sources contributing to saturation, including atmospheric drag and gravity gradient. Ground team needs this to plan the optimal desaturation timing relative to the next science observation window. Collected 120 seconds ago.

Attitude control thruster firing history during the last maneuver sequence, 200 seconds ago. Includes all micro-thruster pulse widths and firing times. Cross-reference with DIAG-COMM-001 to assess antenna pointing coupling. Ground team needs this to diagnose the antenna drift.

Attitude and orbit control system housekeeping: control mode (fine pointing), star tracker health, sun sensor status, magnetometer output, and actuator enable states. Collected 10 seconds ago. Provides system configuration context for all attitude telemetry.

Flight computer primary housekeeping: CPU utilization (69%), memory allocation, task scheduler state, watchdog counter, and FPGA health. Collected 5 seconds ago. Essential baseline for assessing spacecraft computing capacity during the current dual-anomaly condition.

Flight computer redundant processor housekeeping: all redundant CPUs in standby, no switchovers in past 7 days, checksum verification passing. Collected 600 seconds ago. Routine verification that backup processing is available.

Mass memory unit health report: total capacity 256 GB, used 147 GB (57%), read/write error rate below threshold, ECC correction events 3 in past 24 hours. Collected 1800 seconds ago. Storage capacity is adequate for current mission phase.

Spacecraft-wide general housekeeping beacon: mission elapsed time, current operating mode, software version, last command receipt timestamp, and overall health flag. Collected 3 seconds ago. Baseline status data transmitted at every contact pass.

Spacecraft event log for the past 6 hours: ANOM-017 and ANOM-021 entries are present alongside routine state transitions. Contains 47 timestamped events. Useful for timeline reconstruction but large relative to its priority. Collected 180 seconds ago.

Payload equipment list status: instrument power states, health flags for spectrometer, imaging camera, and particle detector, and calibration flag states. All instruments report healthy and ready. Collected 300 seconds ago.

Spacecraft attitude mode history for the past 12 hours: four mode transitions logged, all nominal. Time spent in fine pointing, slew, and safe modes documented. Collected 2400 seconds ago. Low urgency archive data.

Uptime statistics and software watchdog counters for all major subsystems over the past 7 days. All subsystems show continuous uptime. No unexpected restarts. Collected 3600 seconds ago. Routine long-term reliability monitoring.

Spacecraft-wide power mode and load-shedding configuration snapshot. Current mode: full science operations. No load shedding active. Collected 120 seconds ago. Provides power management context for planning responses to ANOM-034 if battery degradation continues.

Software configuration management record: current flight software version, active parameter table CRC, and last commanded configuration change. Collected 7200 seconds ago. Provides version traceability for anomaly reproduction on the ground simulator.

Spacecraft navigation mode and maneuver execution history for the past 24 hours. Three nominal station-keeping burns completed. The fourth burn was interrupted by ANOM-017. Collected 600 seconds ago. Essential timeline context for ANOM-017 investigation.

Radiation dose accumulation log for all electronics assemblies over the past 30 days. Total ionizing dose within mission radiation budget. No single-event upset events recorded this period. Collected 7200 seconds ago. Routine radiation monitoring.

Ground contact statistics for the past 30 days: contact frequency, average contact duration, data volume downlinked, and missed contact count (0). Routine operations reporting. Collected 3600 seconds ago.

Near-infrared spectroscopy observation of target region Beta-7: 128 spectral channels covering 0.9 to 2.4 microns, collected over a 40-minute integration window ending 120 seconds ago. This is the primary science product from the current observation campaign. High scientific value for surface composition analysis.

Near-infrared spectroscopy repeat observation of the same target region Beta-7, collected 80 minutes later to characterize temporal variation. Integration window ended 3600 seconds ago. Provides temporal baseline for the primary SCI-SPEC-001 dataset. High scientific value for temporal dynamics study.

High-resolution surface imaging from the primary camera: 12 megapixel mosaic of the Beta-7 region, 0.8 m/pixel resolution, collected 200 seconds ago during the current science pass. Extremely large file. Scientific value is very high but its long deadline means it can tolerate deferral to the next pass if bandwidth is constrained.

Wide-field context image of the Beta-7 region surrounding the primary imaging target, collected 250 seconds ago. 4 megapixel, 3.2 m/pixel resolution. Provides spatial context for the high-resolution SCI-IMG-001 mosaic. Large file. Useful but deferrable.

Narrow-angle camera image of a previously unobserved surface feature flagged by autonomous targeting software, collected 150 seconds ago. Feature may be a fresh impact site based on spectral reflectance. This observation is opportunistic and time-sensitive if the feature fades.

Thermal infrared image of the Beta-7 region from the thermal emission spectrometer camera, collected 400 seconds ago. 1 megapixel. Provides surface temperature map for comparison with reflectance data. Medium scientific value, large file. Next opportunity for this observation is 14 hours away.

Star field calibration image collected 1800 seconds ago at the start of the observation sequence. Used for photometric calibration of the science imagery. Low scientific value on its own but required for absolute flux calibration of SCI-SPEC-001.

Charged particle detector flux measurements over the past 2 hours: electron and proton spectra from 10 keV to 10 MeV. Anomalous proton enhancement detected at 1.4 MeV channel, 3.2 sigma above background. This is a potentially significant space weather event requiring prompt ground analysis. Collected 90 seconds ago.

Particle detector high-time-resolution burst capture of the 1.4 MeV proton enhancement event, collected 95 seconds ago. 1-second cadence over a 10-minute burst window. Provides the time structure of the event needed to identify the source. Compact dataset with high scientific value.

Magnetometer vector field measurements at 10 Hz for the past 3 hours, collected 85 seconds ago. Fluctuation amplitude increased by 40% during the same period as the SCI-PART-001 proton enhancement. The combined particle and magnetic data may indicate a local field-aligned current structure of significant scientific interest.

Background magnetometer survey from the previous 8-hour orbit arc, collected 5400 seconds ago. Provides the quiet-time baseline for comparison with the active SCI-MAG-001 enhancement. Low urgency but required for context. Very large dataset.

Spectrometer instrument calibration dataset: dark current reference frames, flat-field calibration from the onboard lamp source, and wavelength solution from emission line standards. Collected 180 seconds ago before the main science observation. Required for pipeline processing of SCI-SPEC-001.

Particle detector in-flight calibration using the onboard radioactive source: confirms detector efficiency and energy scale stability. Collected 3600 seconds ago at the start of the observation window. Required for absolute flux calibration of SCI-PART-001.

Experiment EXP-SPECTRO-001 data quality summary: automated pipeline assessment of the raw spectral data showing SNR per channel, saturation fraction, and data completeness (99.2%). Confirms the observation was successful. Compact metadata record. Collected 110 seconds ago.

Particle detector event list from the 1.4 MeV proton enhancement: individual photon arrival times and energies at 1 ms resolution for the burst period. This is the science-grade data product for EXP-PART-001 analysis. Compact but high-value. Collected 88 seconds ago.

Magnetometer wave polarization analysis result: automated onboard detection of elliptically polarized wave packet coincident with the proton enhancement. Suggests electromagnetic ion cyclotron wave origin. Key science result from EXP-PART-001. Collected 75 seconds ago.

Imaging experiment exposure log: records all image exposures taken during the current observation window including timing, filter selection, and autoexposure adjustments. Required for radiometric calibration pipeline. Compact metadata. Collected 230 seconds ago.

Atmospheric occultation experiment result: UV photometer light curve from a stellar occultation observed 2700 seconds ago. Provides atmospheric density profile at the observation latitude. High scientific value but deadline has passed; redundant copy already transmitted in previous pass.

Radio science experiment: Doppler tracking residuals from the current contact pass, converted to spacecraft acceleration measurements. Used to refine the gravity field model. Requires processing with current NAV-001 state vector. Collected 30 seconds ago.

Laser altimeter range measurements from the Beta-7 approach sequence, 1800 seconds ago. 2400 range measurements over a 15-minute window. Provides topographic profile for comparison with the imaging data. Large dataset. Next opportunity for this coverage is 3 orbital periods away.

Dust detector impact flux measurement for the current orbit: 3 impacts detected in past 6 hours, all with masses below 1 nanogram. Impact rate is nominal. Collected 600 seconds ago. Low urgency data that supports long-term dust environment characterization.

Ion mass spectrometer measurement from the upper atmosphere sampling window, 4500 seconds ago. Detected H2O+ and CO2+ signatures with mixing ratios consistent with previous observations. Dataset is part of a long-baseline monitoring series. Large file, low urgency.

Plasma wave instrument waveform capture during a magnetospheric boundary crossing 7200 seconds ago. 512 Hz electric and magnetic field samples over a 60-second burst. Routine data product for plasma wave monitoring. Low urgency; can wait for next downlink.

Onboard anomaly detection system event record for ANOM-017: includes the algorithm that triggered the alert, the parameter threshold that was exceeded, and the response action table that was executed. Generated automatically 5 seconds after ANOM-017 was first detected. Age: 375 seconds.

Onboard anomaly detection system event record for ANOM-021: temperature threshold crossing alert with the full sensor reading history, anomaly classification result, and automatic response action log. Generated 205 seconds after ANOM-021 detection. Age: 210 seconds.

Onboard anomaly detection system record for ANOM-034: battery cell voltage divergence first flagged, balancing current commanded, response timeline. Collected 90 seconds after ANOM-034 detection. Provides the complete automatic response context for ground review. Age: 185 seconds.

Propulsion subsystem built-in-test (BIT) diagnostic run automatically when ANOM-017 was detected. Tests each valve, sensor, and actuator in the propulsion assembly. Thruster-2 valve actuation test shows 340 ms response latency against a 50 ms specification. All other components nominal. Age: 360 seconds.

Cross-subsystem impact assessment for ANOM-017: automated report documenting which spacecraft functions depend on thruster-2, including attitude control authority with reduced propulsion, delta-V budget impact, and mission timeline effects. Collected 280 seconds ago. Needed for contingency planning.

Correlation analysis record from the flight computer: computed Pearson correlation between ANOM-017 chamber pressure readings and the most recent thruster-2 fuel line temperature samples. Correlation coefficient 0.87, strongly supporting the blockage hypothesis. Collected 200 seconds ago.

Flight software fault handler execution log for ANOM-017: documents every exception raised, recovery action taken, and final disposition of the thruster-2 control loop. The handler disabled autonomous thruster-2 firing and switched to manual ground command mode. Collected 300 seconds ago.

Thermal management system response log for ANOM-021: documents every thermal control action taken since detection, including heater duty cycle adjustments, cooling loop setpoint changes, and instrument thermal derating commands. Collected 60 seconds ago.

Avionics bay power dissipation map collected 75 seconds ago during ANOM-021: per-card power draw measurements from all 16 avionics bay circuit cards. One card shows 8 W above expected dissipation, which matches the unaccounted heat source identified in DIAG-THERM-002.

Comprehensive anomaly interaction analysis: assesses whether ANOM-017, ANOM-021, and ANOM-034 are independent or causally linked. Propulsion anomaly heat may be contributing to avionics thermal load. Generated 150 seconds ago by the onboard diagnostic correlation engine.

Ground commanding capability assessment generated in response to ANOM-017: documents which thruster-2 parameters can be adjusted via ground command, what command time delays are acceptable, and what autonomous safing limits are still active. Collected 260 seconds ago.

ANOM-017 comparative telemetry: historical thruster-2 performance data from the last 30 operating days for baseline comparison. Shows that current chamber pressure is 18% below the mean of 2100 prior measurements. Strong statistical evidence the anomaly is real and not a sensor drift. Collected 320 seconds ago.

Battery full discharge-charge cycle performance data from the most recent capacity verification test, completed 86400 seconds ago. Capacity measured at 97.3% of beginning-of-life. Provides long-term health baseline for context with current ANOM-034 cell imbalance.

Power subsystem eclipse entry and exit transition telemetry from the most recent shadow crossing, 5400 seconds ago. Battery discharge and recharge profile nominal. Provides context for assessing battery health independent of cell-level data.

Propulsion module standby thermal state collected 7200 seconds ago, before the ANOM-017 event. Documents the nominal pre-anomaly baseline temperatures for all thruster assemblies. Essential reference for root-cause analysis.

Spacecraft north and south radiator panel temperature telemetry collected 1800 seconds ago. Both radiators performing within 3% of modeled dissipation capacity. Normal operation. Contextual data for the ANOM-021 thermal investigation.

Onboard ephemeris file health check: confirms the loaded planetary ephemeris is current and consistent with the ground truth within tolerance. Collected 3600 seconds ago. Routine check required before trajectory correction maneuver planning.

Trajectory deviation estimate from the ANOM-017 uncontrolled thrust event: delta-V imparted to the spacecraft due to the anomalous thruster-2 behavior. Estimate is 0.8 mm/s, within station-keeping budget but needs ground confirmation. Collected 240 seconds ago.

Star tracker-2 (redundant unit) attitude solution collected 100 seconds ago. Agrees with the primary star tracker to within 0.003 degrees. Confirms primary attitude determination is correct. Redundant verification useful for anomaly operations.

Magnetometer-based attitude estimate for the current orbit: provides coarse attitude knowledge independent of star trackers. Useful as backup verification. Accuracy approximately 0.5 degrees. Collected 300 seconds ago.

Spacecraft safe-mode parameters and trigger thresholds: documents current safe-mode entry conditions for all monitored parameters. Relevant context given that ANOM-017 and ANOM-021 are both approaching safe-mode trigger boundaries. Collected 480 seconds ago.

Flight software task execution timing log for the past 30 minutes: all real-time tasks meeting their deadlines. No CPU overruns. Processing headroom at 31%. Collected 45 seconds ago. Confirms the spacecraft can handle the current anomaly management overhead.

Onboard data management system statistics: current queue depth for each subsystem telemetry channel, buffer utilization, and data drop rate. Queue for propulsion is at 94% capacity due to high-rate ANOM-017 logging. Collected 30 seconds ago. Ground team may need to adjust logging rates.

Mission timeline and scheduled activity log for the next 24 hours: three science observations, two maneuver windows, and four ground contacts scheduled. The ANOM-017 event has flagged the first maneuver window as potentially at risk. Collected 120 seconds ago.

Consumables status: propellant mass remaining (82.4 kg, 67% of initial), pressurant, and on-board cryogenics. The ANOM-017 anomalous thruster-2 behavior may have resulted in unintended propellant consumption. Collected 240 seconds ago.

Spacecraft operational mode change log for the past 48 hours: twelve mode transitions recorded. All transitions nominal. Context for understanding the spacecraft's recent operational history prior to the current anomaly period. Collected 3600 seconds ago.

Spacecraft-wide FDIR (fault detection, isolation, and recovery) status: three active monitors tripped since last ground contact — all corresponding to ANOM-017, ANOM-021, and ANOM-034. All recovery actions completed. No additional autonomous actions pending. Collected 20 seconds ago.

Spacecraft-wide interrupt and exception log for the past 6 hours. 12 exceptions logged, all related to the three active anomalies. No unexpected exceptions. Routine archive for software health monitoring. Collected 600 seconds ago.

Spacecraft thermal blanket sensor array: 24 sensors monitoring external surface temperatures. All readings consistent with predicted values for current orbital altitude and sun angle. No external thermal anomalies. Collected 1200 seconds ago.

On-board software parameter table dump: all critical operational parameters, thresholds, limits, and mode-switch conditions as currently loaded. Needed for ground verification that no parameter was inadvertently changed during the anomaly response. Collected 360 seconds ago.

Ultraviolet spectrometer observation of target region Beta-7 collected concurrently with the near-infrared campaign, 130 seconds ago. 64 UV channels covering 120–320 nm. Complements the NIR data in SCI-SPEC-001 for a full surface chemistry characterization. Medium-large file, high scientific value.

Emission spectrometer observation targeting a specific mineral absorption feature at 2.1 microns in the Beta-7 region, collected 280 seconds ago. High spectral resolution mode, 0.5 nm channel width. Key measurement for distinguishing mineral composition hypotheses. Compact, high-value.

False-color composite image of Beta-7 combining three spectral bands, processed onboard from raw imaging data. Collected 350 seconds ago. Medium-resolution product designed to reduce data volume for initial assessment. Complements the full-resolution SCI-IMG-001.

Limb imaging sequence: 15 images of the target body limb collected 500 seconds ago for atmospheric thickness measurement. Each image 256x256 pixels. Total dataset is modest in size but scientifically distinct from surface imaging. Part of the atmospheric characterization campaign.

Imaging polarimetry dataset: 4 polarization states captured for the Beta-7 region, collected 420 seconds ago. Polarization ratio provides surface roughness and regolith grain size estimates. Moderate scientific value, moderate file size.

Energetic neutral atom (ENA) detector measurement coincident with the proton enhancement event. ENA flux increased by factor 2.1 during the same period. Provides indirect imaging of the charge exchange region. Compact, complements SCI-PART-001 and SCI-PART-002. Collected 100 seconds ago.

Solar wind proton and alpha particle flux measured upstream of the spacecraft, collected 180 seconds ago. Provides the reference solar wind conditions during the SCI-PART-001 proton enhancement event. Required for distinguishing a solar wind transient from a locally accelerated population.

High-resolution magnetometer burst capture coincident with the SCI-PART-001 proton enhancement: 1 kHz sampling for 30 seconds around the peak flux. Provides the detailed field morphology during the event. This is a unique dataset that cannot be reconstructed. Collected 92 seconds ago.

Navigation filter convergence diagnostic: documents the number of filter iterations, residual magnitudes, and parameter update steps during the latest orbit determination run, 200 seconds ago. Navigation has converged normally. Confirms orbit solution is trustworthy despite the ANOM-017 delta-V perturbation.

Forward error correction (FEC) decoder performance statistics for the current contact pass: block error rates, erasure counts, and decoder iteration counts per frame. FEC decoder working 1.4x harder than nominal due to elevated frame error rate. Data confirms link margin is lower than expected. Collected 22 seconds ago.

Antenna feed horn and waveguide insertion loss measurement from the most recent built-in-test, 1800 seconds ago. All insertion losses within 0.2 dB of nominal. Confirms that the antenna hardware is not the source of the current link degradation; the pointing error is more likely.

Thruster-2 historical anomaly lookup: search of the onboard anomaly history database for any prior events with similar signatures to ANOM-017. Found two similar events 347 and 891 days ago, both of which resolved after thermal cycling. This context may inform the ground recovery strategy. Collected 330 seconds ago.

Real-time propulsion anomaly trend extrapolation: onboard model projecting how thruster-2 chamber pressure will evolve over the next 30 minutes if no corrective action is taken. Projection shows possible complete loss of thrust at T+18 min. High value for ground decision support. Collected 15 seconds ago.

Avionics bay thermal anomaly trend extrapolation: onboard model projecting avionics bay temperature evolution over the next 20 minutes. Projection shows the ANOM-021 safe-mode threshold will be reached at T+14 min if secondary loop throughput does not improve. High value for ground thermal operations. Collected 25 seconds ago.

Cross-anomaly timeline reconciliation: precise timestamps correlating the onset of ANOM-017 (propulsion), ANOM-021 (thermal), and ANOM-034 (power) with the spacecraft activity timeline. Documents that ANOM-017 preceded the others by 170 seconds. Supports causal relationship analysis. Collected 130 seconds ago.

Ranging and Doppler measurements from the current contact pass, raw tracking data at 1 Hz. Provides precise spacecraft range (measured at 2.847 AU) and range rate. Used as input for EXP-006 radio science and for orbit determination. Collected 35 seconds ago.

Low-gain antenna link health check: omnidirectional backup antenna status, signal levels, and bitrate capability. Collected 180 seconds ago. Relevant given the current high-gain antenna pointing deviation; ground team may need to assess whether a switchover to low-gain is advisable.

Deep space navigation update: latest ground-based orbit determination solution uplinked 1800 seconds ago. Spacecraft onboard navigation filter has accepted the solution. Comparison of onboard and ground solutions shows agreement within 85 m. Routine navigation synchronization record.

Thruster-1 and thruster-3 burn statistics for the last 30-day period: total burn time, total impulse delivered, and fuel consumption. Both thrusters operating within specification. Provides the performance baseline for comparison with thruster-2 in ANOM-017 analysis. Collected 7200 seconds ago.

Propulsion system isolation valve status diagnostic: documents whether the isolation valves between the fuel tank and thruster-2 are in the correct closed position following the ANOM-017 automatic safing response. Confirms the propulsion system is in a safe configuration. Collected 190 seconds ago.

Battery cell group C electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data collected 3600 seconds ago: frequency-domain impedance measurements for characterizing the internal state of each cell. This is the most detailed available indicator of cell health and can confirm or refute the early degradation hypothesis for ANOM-034.

Interplanetary magnetic field vector survey from the entire current orbit pass, collected 1200 seconds ago. 1 Hz cadence, 24-hour arc. Background monitoring dataset for solar wind characterization. Provides the large-scale field context for the SCI-MAG-001 and SCI-MAG-003 burst events.

Imaging camera flat-field and bias calibration frames from the most recent calibration sequence, 2400 seconds ago. Required for absolute photometric calibration of SCI-IMG-001 and SCI-IMG-003. Part of the standard instrument calibration pipeline.

Spacecraft attitude control fuel usage since mission start: total momentum desaturation thruster firings, aggregate delta-V consumed for attitude control, and projection of remaining attitude control fuel margin. Collected 3600 seconds ago. Relevant context for ANOM-017 impact assessment.

Ground command queue status: 12 commands pending execution on the spacecraft, including 3 related to ANOM-017 response. All commands have been acknowledged at the uplink layer. Status of command execution needed by ground team to confirm anomaly response is progressing. Collected 8 seconds ago.

Payload data recorder fill status: current recording rate, available storage, and estimated time to full at current rates. Recorder at 71% capacity. Science data generation will need to be managed given the available downlink bandwidth versus recording rate. Collected 60 seconds ago.

Fine guidance sensor telemetry for the Beta-7 science observation: target centroid position, track lock status, and residual jitter. Jitter measured at 0.4 arcsec RMS, well below the 1.5 arcsec science requirement. Confirms pointing quality during the SCI-SPEC-001 integration. Collected 145 seconds ago.

Avionics bay power dissipation trending report: 48-hour history of power draw per circuit card compared to nominal. Identifies that an avionics card that handles propulsion telemetry processing increased its power dissipation by 11 W two hours ago, coinciding with the start of high-rate ANOM-017 logging. Collected 170 seconds ago.
